title: calibrated-config

schemaVersion.description: Schema version this document conforms to (semver).

profile.description: Profile name the calibration was run under, e.g. field-app.

correctness_bar.description: How rigorous correctness guarantees must be. Rises with money transactions or critical data provenance.

sensitivity.description: How careful to be with the data. Intrinsic to the domain; scales hook severity at generation time.

infra.description: Deployment target for the app. Proposed by the engine from the decision rules in SPEC §4.1, decided by the owner (recorded in decisions.infra), and realized by the matching deploy profile (SPEC §4.2). vercel: request/response Next.js apps, lowest ops. railway: apps that need a long-lived process (workers, websockets, cron) or flat predictable cost. aws / gcp: an existing client cloud, a compliance or residency regime, private networking, or a large scale horizon — always with infrastructure as code. self-hosted: data that may not leave client premises; needs high ops capacity.

runtime.description: Per-app runtime. ts-nextjs is the default for product/UI apps; python for small backend APIs, ML workflows, and data pipelines.

topology.description: Repo shape. monorepo when the project spans multiple apps (one monorepo per client project).

dials.description: The resolved calibration dials for the app.

invariants.description: Named invariants to enforce (exact-match keys, e.g. observations_append_only_never_delete).

patterns.description: Named stack patterns to inject, e.g. nextjs-app-router.

estimated_infra_monthly_usd.description: Estimated monthly infrastructure cost in USD.

risk_assessment.description: Feasibility, cost, and timeline assessment for the calibrated app.

rationale.description: Why that rule fired, in a sentence, with the inputs it read.

anyOf.description: Deployment target for the app. Proposed by the engine from the decision rules in SPEC §4.1, decided by the owner (recorded in decisions.infra), and realized by the matching deploy profile (SPEC §4.2). vercel: request/response Next.js apps, lowest ops. railway: apps that need a long-lived process (workers, websockets, cron) or flat predictable cost. aws / gcp: an existing client cloud, a compliance or residency regime, private networking, or a large scale horizon — always with infrastructure as code. self-hosted: data that may not leave client premises; needs high ops capacity.

runner_up.description: The next-best admissible target — the alternative the owner is declining.

unanswered.description: §4.1 inputs the intake profile could not answer; the owner weighs them before deciding.

status.description: proposed = awaiting the owner; decided = the owner has accepted or overridden.

anyOf.description: Deployment target for the app. Proposed by the engine from the decision rules in SPEC §4.1, decided by the owner (recorded in decisions.infra), and realized by the matching deploy profile (SPEC §4.2). vercel: request/response Next.js apps, lowest ops. railway: apps that need a long-lived process (workers, websockets, cron) or flat predictable cost. aws / gcp: an existing client cloud, a compliance or residency regime, private networking, or a large scale horizon — always with infrastructure as code. self-hosted: data that may not leave client premises; needs high ops capacity.

decided.description: The owner’s decision, once made. Equals `dials.infra` when decided.

decided_by.description: Only a human decides the deploy target. The engine proposes.

note.description: The owner’s reason, recorded for the decision log.

infra.description: Deploy-target decision record: what the engine proposed, and what the owner decided (SPEC §4.1).

decisions.description: Decisions the engine proposes but a human makes. Each carries the proposal and the decision side by side.

description: The calibrated configuration produced from an intake profile: dials, invariants, patterns, risk, and the propose/decide records.
